changes: pads: none → pads (groove_mm 3, lip_mm 0, pad_angle_deg 20, pad_tpu_mm 2, reach_mm 0, width_mm 12)
why: This is the cheapest fix. All items are on hand: m2 screws and about 18 machine minutes of PLA+TPU printing, so $0 and no lead time. With a 20 deg pad, the leftover tilt is about 28 deg on the gelatin box (tan 0.53, well under 0.9) and about 10-12 deg on the tennis ball and apple. At 17 mm the pad is about 19 deg off the other way (bottom in). tan(19 deg) = 0.34, still far under 0.9, so small objects stay held. No params move can do this: System 1 already searched every grasp setting, and the face tilt is set by geometry at each width.

No trial has changed groove and width alone. The two trials that touched them also changed pad_angle (lost the banana) or added a lip (lost almost everything to moving_jaw_missed). Those losses are explained by the angle and the lip, not by the groove. Keeping pad_angle at 20 and lip at 0 leaves the tilt profile the banana depends on unchanged. A 5 mm groove on a 20 mm pad gives two flank contacts per jaw that cradle a 47-59 mm sphere across the pad, so it cannot roll out sideways. The thicker 3 mm TPU skin adds compliance. Cost is $0: m2 screws on hand, about 25 machine minutes.

A 3 deg shift moves the parallel point from about 0.35 rad (about 33 mm) to about 0.40 rad (about 36-37 mm). Expected tilts: strawberry 33 mm about 2 deg down (now 5), plum 40-42 mm about 5 deg (now 8-9), racquetball and lemon 46-47 mm about 6-9 deg (now 9-14). Every pad_angle tried so far was 20 or 29-33 (or 18 together with reach 25). The 29 trial with no lip or reach lost only the banana, which means the other held groups tolerate a 9 deg shift. Banana at 35 mm goes from about 2 deg bottom-out to about 1 deg bottom-in, well short of the about 7 deg bottom-in that made it never_lifted at 29. Larger moves cannot be justified: the slide and four-bar jaws (vertical or bottom-in faces) lost the banana every time, and reach lost the potted meat can and the dice. Only the hinge's pad_angle can still move the tilt curve. Cost $0. The reprint takes about 18 machine minutes (2 g PLA plus 1 g TPU per pad set).

At pad_angle 23 the brief puts the face 1 deg off parallel at 35 mm and 6 deg off at 45 mm. Raising pad_angle to 27 moves the parallel point to about 0.47 rad (about 41-42 mm). The plum then closes about parallel, and the racquetball and lemon close about 1-3 deg off instead of 7-9. The bracket is already measured. pad_angle 25 kept every held group in iteration 7, gaining the same strawberry and tomato_soup_can as 23. pad_angle 29 lost the banana (squeezed_up_out). 27 is the untested midpoint, and the cheapest move left that targets this mechanism: no cost and about 18 machine minutes for the reprint. The jaw swaps that remain (prismatic twice, parallelogram three times) have all lost the banana or flat_screwdriver, so I am not repeating them. The 12 V servos would cost $68, over the $40 budget.
